archetype: Explorer bow class whose entire damage engine runs off a two-skill alternation. Cardinal Burst and Cardinal Deluge are cast back to back (via the in-game macro system or the class's own Auto Mode toggle), and that alternation does three jobs at once: it charges the Relic Gauge that every other skill spends, it procs the Bountiful Burst / Bountiful Deluge passives, and it refunds cooldown on the pre-5th-job Ancient Force and Enchant Force skills. Off-burst play is that alternation plus two low-cooldown weave skills. Burst is short and summon-heavy - three summons plus one gauge-consuming nuke inside roughly fifteen seconds - which makes a bind effectively mandatory so the summons connect. Because the main attack is a fixed two-cast macro rather than a keydown or a fast-spam skill, the class scales poorly with attack speed, and because the weave skills are cooldown-gated, it scales unusually well with cooldown reduction and cooldown-skip instead. Only nine skills are boostable, which makes its V Matrix cheap relative to most classes.

linkSkill.name: Adventurer's Curiosity
linkSkill.effect: Passive, shared by all three Explorer Archers and stackable up to three times (once per unique Explorer Archer raised to Master Level on the world). At Master Level 9: Monster Collection registration chance +50%, Critical Rate +15%, Damage +6% (the damage component unlocks at Lv. 7). The wiki notes the Critical Rate bonus applies multiplicatively rather than additively. Grandis Library lists only the Monster Collection and Critical Rate components and omits the +6% Damage - see conflicts.
linkSkill.levels: Master Level 9. Lv. 1 gives Monster Collection +10% / Critical Rate +3%; Lv. 7 adds the Damage component; Lv. 9 reaches +50% / +15% / +6%.

priority.why: Half of the two-cast macro, so its boost multiplies a share of nearly all damage the character deals, bossing and training alike. The class doc puts it in the trio it labels "Bossing (high priority)"; mastermysty lists it in trio #1. The KMS wiki marks it as an "Essential Reinforcing Core" but publishes no priority ordering, so the top-priority ranking rests on two independent lanes, not three. Separately it is the Mastery 1 skill, and the class doc states that to activate a mastery node "the associated boost node level must total at least lvl 40 without matrix points" - so the boost levels have to be built before Mastery 1 can be equipped at all.
priority.sourceCountNote: 2 independent lanes rank it top (class doc, mastermysty). The Mastery-1 grouping and the level-40 gate are separately sourced: the grouping is confirmed by the class doc, the KMS wiki and the GMS wiki (3 lanes); the level-40-without-matrix-points wording is class doc only. Grandis Library also buckets this node (PRIMARY / SECONDARY / OTHER) but its credits block reads 'Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build: Class Doc', so it restates the class doc and is NOT counted as an independent lane.

priority.why: The other half of the macro; the same argument applies. The class doc places it in the same high-priority bossing trio and mastermysty lists it in trio #1. It is the Mastery 2 skill (HEXA Cardinal Deluge + HEXA Bountiful Deluge on the GMS wiki; Cardinal Discharge VI / Additional Discharge VI on the KMS wiki), so it carries the same level-40 boost gate. CORRECTION MADE 2026-09-12: an earlier version of this entry said the KMS wiki "labels this node group the primary one". It does not. The KMS wiki's reinforcement-core table has a column that machine-translates to Primary / Secondary / tertiary / 4th / hyper, and that column is the JOB ADVANCEMENT TIER of each skill, not a priority ranking - Cardinal Deluge is the 1st job attack, which is why its row reads "Primary", while Cardinal Burst (2nd job) reads "Secondary". The KMS wiki publishes no boost node priority order for this class.
priority.sourceCountNote: 2 independent lanes for the priority ranking (class doc, mastermysty). Grandis Library also buckets this node (PRIMARY / SECONDARY / OTHER) but its credits block reads 'Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build: Class Doc', so it restates the class doc and is NOT counted as an independent lane.

priority.why: The higher-priority of the two off-burst weave skills. The class doc's DPM skill priority list runs 1. Glyph, 2. Combo Assault, 3. macro, and it says Glyph is technically ahead because it has no cast time while adding that "in practice Glyph and CA are the same priority". Both supporting facts were re-checked in the doc's skill entry: "It can be cast even while in animation for other skills" and "Outside of burst, this is the main skill that helps you regulate the relic gauge". Present in the first trio in both independent trio lanes, and it is one of the three Mastery 3 skills.
priority.sourceCountNote: 2 independent lanes place it in the first trio (class doc, mastermysty); the Mastery 3 grouping is 3-lane (class doc, KMS wiki, GMS wiki). Grandis Library also buckets this node (PRIMARY / SECONDARY / OTHER) but its credits block reads 'Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build: Class Doc', so it restates the class doc and is NOT counted as an independent lane.

priority.why: The second off-burst weave skill, joint-first with Glyph in the class doc's DPM skill priority ("in practice Glyph and CA are the same priority"). That is a skill-USE priority, not a node priority. As a node it matters because Combo Assault is a Mastery 4 skill: the class doc says in writing "To unlock M3/M4, you must boost Combo Assault, Cardinal Torrent, Ancient Astra, and Shadow Raven", and the KMS and GMS wikis both group it into Mastery Core 4. The class doc also records the Mastery upgrade as the largest single jump on the class (7930% to 30132% skill damage at Lv. 30, cooldown cut to 15s), which is what moved Combo Assault out of mobbing and into the bossing rotation. CAUTION: Grandis Library buckets this node SECONDARY and defines SECONDARY as "Boost Nodes that don't unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery". That is stale (Grandis is tagged GMS Ver. 269) and wrong at v.271, because this node does unlock Mastery 4. Do not use Grandis' bucket to deprioritise it.
priority.sourceCountNote: The Mastery 4 gate is confirmed by three independent lanes (class doc, KMS wiki, GMS wiki). The DPM-priority claim is class doc only.

priority.why: Boosted for the Mastery 3 gate rather than for its own damage. The class doc names it in its explicit "to unlock M3/M4 you must boost" list, the KMS wiki puts Cardinal Transition VI (its name for Cardinal Torrent VI) inside the Essential Reinforcing Core group for Mastery 3, and the GMS wiki lists HEXA Cardinal Torrent under Mastery Node/Core 3. The skill itself is primarily a teleport - the class doc's keybind table calls it "Teleport, limited charges" and the KMS wiki footnotes "It may look like a high-speed mobile skill, but it is a teleport skill".

Also boosted for the Mastery 3 gate. Named in the class doc's "to unlock M3/M4 you must boost" list, in the KMS wiki's Essential Reinforcing Core group, and under Mastery Node/Core 3 on the GMS wiki. Used as a survival tool rather than a damage skill: the class doc's keybind table lists Ancient Astra (Burst) as the iframe, and the KMS wiki footnotes that the skill "is more of a survival utility".

Boosted for the Mastery 4 gate. In the class doc's explicit unlock list, in the KMS wiki's Essential Reinforcing Core group (Raven VI), and under Mastery Node/Core 4 on the GMS wiki. The class doc also flags the base skill as "Mobile summon; needed for burst".

Boostable, useful for mobbing, and explicitly NOT required for any Mastery core. The class doc: "Swarm Shot and Triple Impact are not required for 6th job... Swarm Shot is situationally useful for mobbing." The KMS wiki puts Split Mistel (its name for Swarm Shot) under "select strengthening core" rather than Essential Reinforcing Core.
priority.sourceCountNote: Grandis Library also files it under OTHER ("do not need to be upgraded or has least priority") but restates the class doc, so it is not counted.

priority.why: Also boostable and also not required for any Mastery core. The class doc: "Triple Impact is used more often in bossing but only for utility, not damage." The KMS wiki likewise lists Triple Impact under "select strengthening core".
priority.sourceCountNote: Grandis Library also files it under OTHER but restates the class doc, so it is not counted.

trios.label: Bossing / high priority trio
trios.why: The two macro halves plus the top weave skill. The class doc labels this grouping "Bossing (high priority)"; mastermysty lists the same three as its trio #1 (written Cardinal Deluge / Cardinal Burst / Glyph of Impalement). This is the one trio a boss mule needs - the class doc says "basic boss mules just need 1 set of boost nodes (3 skills), out of only 9 boostable skills total".
trios.sourceCountNote: CORRECTION MADE 2026-09-12: Grandis Library was previously cited here and has been removed. Grandis does not publish trios at all - its "Skills Boosted by Each Nodes" table lists which skills sit on each of six nodes (Node 1 = Cardinal Burst + Bountiful Burst, Node 3 = Glyph + Cardinal Torrent + Ancient Astra, and so on), which is the Mastery-core grouping, not this trio composition. It cannot corroborate a trio it does not state, and it credits its boost node build to the class doc regardless.

trios.label: Second trio (historically labelled 'mobbing')
trios.why: Same three skills in both independent lanes, written in different orders (class doc: Cardinal Torrent / Combo Assault / Swarm Shot; mastermysty trio #2: Swarm Shot / Combo Assault / Cardinal Torrent). IMPORTANT: the class doc states that the "Mobbing" label is no longer accurate - "The old classification of 'Mobbing' trio is no longer accurate, but kept for posterity" - because Combo Assault moved into the bossing rotation with its Mastery core and Cardinal Torrent is now boosted for the Mastery 3 gate. Treat the label as legacy.
trios.sourceCountNote: Grandis Library removed from this entry for the reason given on the first trio - it publishes node contents, not trios.

trios.label: Third / tertiary trio
trios.why: Same three skills in both independent lanes, in different written orders (class doc: Ancient Astra / Shadow Raven / Triple Impact; mastermysty trio #3: Triple Impact / Shadow Raven / Ancient Astra). Two of the three (Ancient Astra, Shadow Raven) are Mastery core prerequisites, so this trio stopped being genuinely optional once Mastery 3 and 4 arrived.
trios.sourceCountNote: Grandis Library removed from this entry for the reason given on the first trio.

trios.label: Five-node min-max setup (class doc's own alternative)
skills: Cardinal Burst / Cardinal Deluge / Glyph of Impalement
Cardinal Deluge / Cardinal Burst / Glyph of Impalement
Cardinal Torrent / Combo Assault / Ancient Astra
Shadow Raven / Combo Assault / Ancient Astra
Swarm Shot / Cardinal Torrent / Shadow Raven
trios.why: Because only seven skills are needed for the Mastery cores, the class doc gives a five-node arrangement covering all seven instead of the six nodes needed to cover all nine, freeing a matrix slot. The doc presents it as optional min-maxing ("For V Matrix min-maxers (not necessary)"), not the default. Re-verified line for line 2026-09-12; the doc's own fourth line contains the typo "Ancient Anstra", corrected to Ancient Astra here.

vMatrix.notes: Nine boostable skills total, needing six node slots to cover all nine, or five slots if you skip Swarm Shot and Triple Impact. The class doc treats the small boostable pool as a selling point and says "If you are planning to unlock 6th job, it is recommended to boost every skill". Mechanics restated by the doc for newcomers: each skill gains boost levels equal to the node's level (up to +25 from node level plus +5 from matrix slot enhancement, cap 60), so each skill must sit on at least two nodes to reach 60; and two nodes cannot be equipped together if they share the same FIRST-line skill, though the same skill in a non-first position is fine. Node LEVELING priority is a separate question from node composition: the doc says boost nodes generally max themselves from opened nodestones, and directs node shards and green EXP nodestones at the class V skills instead, in this order - Raven Tempest, then Nova Blast / Relic Unbound, then Vicious Shot, then Maple World Goddess's Blessing / Erda Nova, then Obsidian Barrier, Guided Arrow, Blink, Rope Lift, Will of Erda, Fury of the Wild. The KMS wiki gives its own V-skill enhancement order and it agrees at both ends but not in the middle: "Ancient Tempest > Relic Unbound > Ultimate Blast > Obsidian Barrier" with a footnote inserting Critical Reinforce (Vicious Shot) and Maple World Goddess' Blessing between Ancient Tempest and Relic Unbound. Both lanes put the Tempest skill first and Obsidian Barrier last; they disagree on where Nova Blast (Ultimate Blast) and Vicious Shot sit. Note also that the doc's list uses the pre-rework names Raven Tempest and Fury of the Wild - see conflicts. The doc also publishes a level-by-level slot unlock order from 200 to 260, then says that order matters much less now that starting matrix slots were raised from 7 to 12 with a 30-slot maximum, and less again since free-EXP changes made reaching 260 fast; its own current advice is "you can just slot in whatever you want after the Bossing trio and the 4 class-specific V skills, then fix up your V Matrix when you do reach 260".

order.step: Mastery core 4 first - Combo Assault VI / Shadow Raven VI / Manifest Curse
order.why: Two independent lanes put Mastery 4 first. The class doc's HEXA leveling chart opens "M4, M1, M2, M3, M3", and the KMS wiki states separately that "the priority for strengthening the Mastery Core is Combo Assault > Edge of Resonance > Cardinal Blast > Cardinal Discharge" - Combo Assault (M4) first in both. Both lanes give the same reason shape: the class doc calls the Combo Assault upgrade the single largest Mastery jump (7930% to 30132% skill damage at Lv. 30, cooldown cut to 15s, promoting it from a mobbing skill into the bossing rotation), and the KMS wiki adds that Manifest Curse / Relic Materialize, the passive that rides along with this core, is worth taking to level 1 even on a low-spec character because it triggers on every Relic Gauge consumption.

order.step: Mastery core 1 - Cardinal Burst VI / Bountiful Burst VI
order.why: Second entry in the class doc's chart order. The doc records a roughly 27% larger hitbox on Cardinal Burst VI and a Bountiful Burst proc rate rising to 50% (base 41%, +1% per 3 levels). CONTESTED POSITION: the KMS wiki's own mastery order places this THIRD, after Combo Assault and Edge of Resonance (Glyph). See conflicts.

order.step: Mastery core 2 - Cardinal Deluge VI / Bountiful Deluge VI
order.why: Third entry in the class doc's chart order; the other macro half. The doc records Bountiful Deluge VI at a 45% proc rate with one extra magical arrow, and a 30% final-damage reduction applied from the second Deluge arrow onward on the same target. CONTESTED POSITION: the KMS wiki places this last of the four. See conflicts.

order.step: Mastery core 3 - Glyph of Impalement VI / Cardinal Torrent VI / Ancient Astra VI (fourth and fifth entries both go here)
order.why: The class doc's stated first-five sequence ends with Mastery 3 twice, so two consecutive investment steps land on this core. Glyph of Impalement VI is the payload: casts of Glyph periodically become an enhanced version, Ancient Impact, and the doc gives 10740% for Glyph and 16110% for Ancient Impact at Lv. 30. CONTESTED POSITION: the KMS wiki puts Edge of Resonance (its name for Glyph) SECOND, immediately after Combo Assault, not fourth. The three sources also disagree on how often Ancient Impact procs - class doc says every 5th cast, KMS wiki says every 4th, and the GMS wiki's own skill text reads "Enhances Glyph of Impalement after being used 2 times" (i.e. every 3rd cast). See conflicts; do not present a cast count as settled.
order.sourceCountNote: Ordering is class doc only and is contradicted by the KMS wiki. The Mastery 3 membership (Glyph, Cardinal Torrent, Ancient Astra) is separately 3-lane: class doc, KMS wiki, GMS wiki.

skillCore.note: The GMS wiki lists exactly two skill cores for Pathfinder at v.271, labelled in its own words "Skill Node/Core 1 (Origin) - Forsaken Relic" and "Skill Node/Core 2 (Ascent) - Piercing Relic". The class doc describes Forsaken Relic only (a 10s Absolute Bind, an invulnerable cutscene, a 30s Relic Liberation buff giving up to 15% final damage to Ancient and Enchant Force skills, and a triggered Ancient Wrath effect) and does NOT cover Piercing Relic at all - that is a real gap in the doc. RESOLVED 2026-09-12: the earlier note said the KMS wiki lists a THIRD skill core and that whether GMS has it was unconfirmed. The KMS wiki does list a third entry under its skill-core heading (machine-translated as "material burst"), but its GMS / MSEA / JMS name fields are blank, and the GMS wiki - edited on the v.271 patch date - lists only the two above. Treat GMS as having two skill cores. Note also that the KMS wiki calls the Ascent skill "Relic Penetion"/"Relic Penetration" (MSEA string); the GMS string is Piercing Relic.
skillCore.sourceCountNote: Split evidence, so labelled to the weakest part. Forsaken Relic as the Origin core is 3-lane (class doc, KMS wiki, GMS wiki). The existence and position of the Ascent core is 2-lane (KMS wiki, GMS wiki). Its GMS string Piercing Relic is GMS-wiki-only - the KMS wiki gives only the MSEA form Relic Penetration and the class doc does not mention the skill at all.

mastery.unlockRule: The class doc states it plainly: "In order to activate mastery nodes, the associated boost node level must total at least lvl 40 without matrix points." That is the practical link between the V Matrix section and this one - matrix slot enhancement points do not count toward the 40. The doc separately names which skills that means in practice: "To unlock M3/M4, you must boost Combo Assault, Cardinal Torrent, Ancient Astra, and Shadow Raven" (Cardinal Burst, Cardinal Deluge and Glyph are already in the bossing trio).
mastery.unlockRuleNote: The level-40 figure and the without-matrix-points qualifier come from the class doc alone; neither wiki states a numeric gate. The membership of the four cores, by contrast, is three-lane.

enhancement.note: Four enhancement nodes; names taken verbatim from the GMS wiki's HEXA Enhancements table and matched against the KMS wiki. Three of them (Nova Blast, Tempest, Relic Unbound) are pure final damage with no added effect; only Obsidian Barrier gains functionality - the class doc records its duration rising to 20s (base 13s at Lv. 1, +1s per 4 levels) and its damage reduction rising to 55% (base 41%, +1% per 2 levels). The GMS wiki states the prerequisite: "Enhancements require the corresponding V Skill to be leveled to max and equipped." The final-damage curve is 11% at Lv. 1, 25% at 10, 40% at 20, 60% at 30 - the class doc, the GMS wiki and the KMS wiki all give the same breakpoints. NOTE: the class doc still lists this node as "Raven Tempest"; both wikis name it Ancient Tempest/Primal Tempest - see conflicts.

common.note: The class doc states flatly that Sol Janus "has no bossing function. It's purely for lazier farming and increased %EXP" and leaves the investment level to the player, while the doc's current owner (Naicha) is quoted arguing for maxing it as soon as possible on the grounds that faster levelling compounds into earlier boss progression and therefore more gear. The GMS wiki corroborates the mechanical half of that independently: "All forms of Sol Janus cannot be used on boss maps." For Sol Hecate the doc gives two binding recommendations: bind Styx to AB activation - and also keep it on its own key so it can be fired earlier - and bind Phlegethon to any 2-minute skill, preferring one already in the skill sequence "(like Bubble)" because the boss is most likely to be bound at that moment. CORRECTION MADE 2026-09-12: an earlier version read "bind Styx to Awakened Relic activation". AB in this doc means the Angelic Buster link skill, not Awakened Relic - the doc uses AB consistently in the phrase "AB + Oz Ring", which it says should always be popped consecutively immediately before the burst skills. "Bubble" is the community nickname for Obsidian Barrier, which the doc's own skill entry describes as summoning a bubble.
common.sourceCountNote: The binding advice for Sol Hecate is class doc only (1 lane). The Sol-Janus-is-not-for-bossing claim has 2 lanes (class doc judgement, GMS wiki mechanic).

hexaStat.heroic: ATT > DEX > Boss Damage / Critical Damage. The class doc writes this as "Heroic: ATT > DEX > BOSS/CDMG" and immediately qualifies it: "Prioritize these stats in order of highest HEXA stat value" - i.e. take whichever line rolls the highest value rather than following a fixed order. It adds that Boss Damage and Critical Damage are close in practice, with Boss Damage generally slightly better for characters without full Eternal gear and boss familiars, and points at maplescouter for a character-specific answer.
hexaStat.interactive: Critical Damage > ATT > Boss Damage > main stat (the doc writes "Interactive: CRITDMG > ATT > BOSS > STAT"). Its stated reason is that Interactive/Regular players have more Stat and ATT available from bonus potentials, which makes Boss Damage and Critical Damage scarcer there. This is NOT the Heroic recommendation - do not apply it to a Reboot character.
hexaStat.sequencing: The class doc says to take a HEXA Stat to level 20 before optimising it, because maxing it is what unlocks HEXA Stat 2 (and the same pattern for HEXA Stat 3); reconfiguring a HEXA Stat setup later costs 100 million mesos. It frames full HEXA Stat optimisation as endgame work "akin to endgame levels like working on legion champion", to be returned to after 6th job is otherwise finished, and suggests saving main-stat HEXA Stat rolls for Sunny Sunday rate-up perks.
hexaStat.whyItIsClassSpecific: Vicious Shot converts critical rate into critical damage, which the class doc says "does greatly diminish crit damage efficiency" - that is the specific reason Critical Damage does not simply sit at the top of the Heroic HEXA Stat order the way it does for many classes. The doc balances it against boss damage being very inflated in the endgame, which is why it calls the two close.

hexa.notes: HONEST LIMIT: this is the weakest-sourced section in this file, and that reflects the public record rather than a shortfall of searching. The class doc is the only source giving a full Pathfinder HEXA investment order, that order lives in an image rather than in text, and the doc credits the image to MapleScouter - a calculator - rather than to independent Pathfinder analysis. Only the first five chart entries are stated in readable text ("The first 5 in the order guide is M4, M1, M2, M3, M3") and only those are recorded above; everything after is unsourced and deliberately left out. NEW 2026-09-12: the KMS wiki does give a mastery-core investment priority of its own - Combo Assault > Edge of Resonance > Cardinal Blast > Cardinal Discharge, i.e. M4 > M3 > M1 > M2. It agrees with the class doc that M4 comes first and disagrees on everything after, which is why only the M4-first step is labelled moderate and the rest stay weak. Three further facts the doc gives: the order it publishes is built for Sol-Erda-Fragment-limited servers, which is the Heroic case; it is optimised for full rotation damage, so a player who cares more about burst damage distribution on specific bosses is told to deviate toward the Origin skill and the Tempest skill; and HEXA Stat 1 and 2 are folded into the same chart rather than being a separate project. The doc also asserts that heavy fragment investment pays off unusually well for this class because "several of its HEXA cores have above-average and/or super-linear scaling" - single-source and unquantified.

hyperStats.orderedNote: BOTH lists below are UNORDERED SETS, not rankings. The class doc introduces them as "the most important stats as a rule of thumb" and gives exactly one allocation rule - "You should typically get all of the most important stats to level 10 before putting more points in a single stat" - and no ranking. Array position here carries NO priority meaning; any consumer that reads index order as priority will be inventing a claim the source declines to make. The order below is simply the order the doc's table prints.
bossingImportantStats: Critical Rate (the class doc says typically leave at lvl 8-10)
mobbingImportantStats: EXP (max if you don't need more damage)
Arcane Force (only if you need to hit a threshold)
hyperStats.notes: The class doc deliberately refuses to publish a ranked hyper stat order. Its stated grounds: "Your personal Hyper Stats will always vary based on your equipment and level", followed by "Please use maplescouter (or similar) to optimize your own Hyper Stats." That refusal is itself the finding and should be surfaced to users rather than replaced with a manufactured list. The only general rule the doc gives is the level-10-across-the-board rule quoted above. The 'priority' field is null on purpose: no source consulted publishes a defensible fixed ranking for Pathfinder, and Grandis Library carries no hyper stat guidance at all. Re-verified against the doc's Hyper Skills / Hyper Stats section on 2026-09-12; both lists match the doc's table item for item.

alwaysTake.why: The class doc lists these three under the heading "You should always take these"; the remaining two of the five slots are conditional (see conditionalLastTwo). All three names were validated against the GMS wiki's Hyper Skills table, which confirms the effects: Extra Strike adds +1 attack to Cardinal Force skills, Bountiful Enhance adds +10% activation chance to Bountiful Deluge and Bountiful Burst, and Boss Rush gives +20% Boss Damage to "Ancient Force and Enchant Force skills". Grandis Library's flat five-pick list contains all three, but Grandis credits its hyper passive build to the Class Doc, so that is one source agreeing with itself and it is not counted as a second lane.
alwaysTake.sourceCountNote: 1 independent judgement lane (the class doc). The GMS wiki is used only to validate the skill names and effect text - it makes no recommendation. Grandis Library restates the class doc by its own credits block.

conditionalLastTwo.rule: The final two passive picks depend on the character's IED and cooldown-reduction hat, per a table in the class doc. Re-read verbatim 2026-09-12: the table's axes are CD Hat ("-2s or less" / "-3s or more") against IED ("< 98.2" / "> 98.2"), and the > 98.2 row gives one answer spanning both hat columns.

cases.condition: IED below 98.2% AND cooldown hat of -2s or less
IED below 98.2% AND cooldown hat of -3s or more

conditionalLastTwo.note: Grandis Library publishes only the first of these three cases, as a flat five-pick list (Reinforce, Bountiful Enhance, Extra Strike, Boss Rush, Guardbreak), with no mention that the last two are conditional. If MaplePlanner presents a static five-pick list it will be silently wrong for two of the three cases. The reason Boss Rush and Guardbreak are weighted so highly is confirmed on the GMS wiki's own skill text: both are described as applying to "Ancient Force and Enchant Force skills", not to Ancient Force alone.
conditionalLastTwo.sourceCountNote: The conditional table exists in one source only - the class doc. Grandis restates one case of it and credits the class doc; the GMS wiki supplies effect text but no build advice.

actives.note: The class doc's required-keybind table lists both under the Hyper heading: Ancient Astra (Burst) with the note "iframe", and Awakened Relic with the note "Needed for burst". Elsewhere the doc records that Awakened Relic instantly fills the Relic Gauge and cuts Cardinal Torrent's stack recharge from 7s to 3s for 30s - both confirmed on the GMS wiki's skill text. CORRECTION MADE 2026-09-12: an earlier version described Ancient Astra as "the iframe / 60% damage reduction tool", conflating two different stances. Per the GMS wiki, the 60% damage reduction belongs to Ancient Astra (Deluge), which applies it while channelling; the class doc's iframe note is about Ancient Astra in Burst mode, which it elsewhere puts at 2s of iframe. SECOND CORRECTION: an earlier version said Epic Adventure "is listed by the KMS wiki as the third hyper active" and implied it is absent from GMS sources. It is listed as a hyper active on BOTH wikis, including the GMS wiki. What is true is that the class doc does not discuss it.
actives.sourceCountNote: Both wikis list the same three hyper actives (Awakened Relic, Ancient Astra, Epic Adventure) - that part is 2-lane. The judgement that Ancient Astra and Awakened Relic are the required keybinds is class doc only.

fullActiveList.note: The complete hyper active list for the class, per both wikis. Epic Adventure is the shared Explorer hyper active; neither the class doc nor Grandis Library discusses it.

bossing.line: Chance to skip cooldowns +20% (top line, Legendary)
bossing.why: Two independent lanes agree and give the same mechanical reason. The class doc lists it as the first of its three bossing lines and tells you to roll it LAST in practice because the top line is cheap to obtain and re-obtain. The KMS wiki argues it from mechanics: before 6th job it is "not a very good option", but after 6th job "Edge of Resonance VI is strengthened with Ancient Impact every 4 times and Relic Materialize stacks and deals additional hits every time 50 Relic Gauge is consumed", so once the Mastery cores are open it becomes "an option that must be given priority". Both effects scale with cast frequency, and Pathfinder's off-burst damage is two cooldown-gated weave skills whose cooldowns are already being refunded by macro casts, so a skip converts almost directly into extra weave casts. The KMS wiki also recommends taking it at Legendary rather than Unique grade "since the Unique grade has a low probability of being reset".
bossing.sourceCountNote: 2 independent lanes (class doc, KMS wiki). Grandis Library lists the same three bossing lines but credits its Inner Ability build to the Class Doc, so it is not a third opinion. One aggregator dissents - see conflicts.

bossing.line: Critical Rate +20% (Unique line, second or third slot)
bossing.why: Both independent lanes flag this as worth more to Pathfinder than to a typical class, for the same reason: Vicious Shot (Critical Reinforce) converts total critical rate - including the portion above 100% - into critical damage, so the line keeps paying after the crit cap. The class doc says to "prioritize rolling for Unique Crit Rate as this is the most difficult line to get". The KMS wiki puts a figure on it - "equivalent to 10% CDM at extreme damage" - and argues that because it is worth less than a 20% ATT line it should sit "as a unique in the second row or lower", which is consistent with the class doc putting cooldown skip on top.
bossing.sourceCountNote: 2 independent lanes (class doc, KMS wiki); Grandis restates the class doc.

bossing.line: Boss Damage +10% (Unique line), with +8% damage to enemies afflicted by an abnormal status as an accepted settle
bossing.why: The class doc's other Unique line, and it says explicitly "You can settle Abnormal Status Damage over Boss Damage on the other Unique line." The KMS wiki independently argues the abnormal-status line is actually the better of the two on the lower slots for this class, because "status ailments can be easily inflicted with the ancient curse debuff or the adventurer wizard link skill" so the condition is effectively always met, and because the first line only reaches 10% while the 2nd and 3rd lines reach 8%, making the lower lines proportionally more efficient. It caveats that "if the cooldown is used as the first line, the efficiency is inferior".
bossing.sourceCountNote: 2 independent lanes (class doc, KMS wiki); Grandis restates the class doc.

training.sourceCountNote: Class doc only as a judgement lane; Grandis prints the same three training lines but credits the class doc. The KMS wiki lists drop rate / meso obtained as a hunting preset without ranking.
Class doc only as a judgement lane; Grandis restates it. The doc also says the two may be swapped.

training.line: +8% damage to normal monsters (the class doc calls this line optional)
training.sourceCountNote: Class doc only; its exact words are "Normal Monster Damage is optional; the third line is not that important."

rollingStrategy.heroic: The class doc gives a Heroic-specific sequence, re-read verbatim 2026-09-12: use Miracle Circulators to reach Unique Critical Rate first (Interactive players can consider raw rolling for it, ideally during a 50%-off Inner Ability event); lock that line and roll for Unique Boss Damage, settling for Abnormal Status Damage if needed; once both Unique lines are present, use Chaos or Black Circulators from seasonal event shops to max their values, ideally before touching the top line; then lock both Unique lines and roll the top line last, because the top line is "relatively cheap but also the biggest gain" and easy to re-obtain.
rollingStrategy.alternative: The doc offers a second approach - settle one preset on something workable and roll a different preset freely for perfect lines, which avoids bricking a usable setup at the cost of an extra preset and probably more total Honor.
rollingStrategy.newPlayers: The doc is explicit: "NEW PLAYERS: settle on any usable line(s), even if it's only Legendary Boss Damage or CD Skip. You do not need to minmax the Unique lines while in early/mid game."
practicalNotes: Keep 20% Item Drop Rate on some preset for boss reward room drops.
Only roll during 50% Honor cost events - the doc calls this strongly recommended.
Use seasonal event shops for Circulators and Honor Medals.

The class doc notes that a heavy farmer is usually better served by Legendary Mesos Obtained plus a third preset carrying only 20% Item Drop Rate, while a light farmer or low-Honor player should just take a single Legendary Item Drop Rate line.

The KMS wiki adds a line the GMS doc does not: buff duration (up to 38% on a second row or lower line) is worth considering for a low-Honor character because it applies to the Angelic Buster link skill.

The class doc adds an Interactive-server-only note: "if you own a FSR, CD skip affects this as well to make it even more valuable (unless you need the 8% Damage to 1-shot with Erda Shower/Sol Janus)". The doc does not expand the abbreviation FSR and it is not expanded here.
rollingStrategy.sourceCountNote: The rolling sequence itself is class doc only; the buff-duration addendum is KMS wiki only. No claim here has two lanes behind it, hence weak.

innerAbility.notes: Note the shape of this class's Inner Ability: a cooldown-skip top line plus a cooldown-reduction hat is an unusually expensive combination, and the class doc lists that requirement in its own cons section as a funding barrier. One cross-class aggregator disagrees on the top line; see conflicts, where the asymmetry between it and the two class-specific lanes is set out.

gearingNotes: CRITICAL RATE DOES NOT STOP MATTERING AT 100%. Vicious Shot converts up to 50% of the character's total critical rate - explicitly including the portion above 100% - into critical damage for 30 seconds. Two independent lanes (the GMS class doc and the KMS wiki) state this and both draw the same two conclusions from it: keep buying critical rate past the cap, and discount other sources of percentage critical damage, because the class doc says Vicious Shot dilutes the value of critical damage from glove potential and pitched set bonuses relative to a non-Archer class. This is the single most important class-specific gearing fact for Pathfinder and it propagates into hyper stats, Inner Ability, Legion and HEXA Stat. COOLDOWN IS THIS CLASS'S SCALING STAT. The class doc's cooldown-reduction section was rewritten after the GMS March 2026 balance patch and now says a -4s hat or better is best-in-slot; on Reboot take anything -4s or better because the server only has bright cubes, while GMS Regular sees the largest gain from a -6s to -8s hat. Combined with the cooldown-skip Inner Ability line, this is what the doc means when it lists 'uncommon (higher funding) setup required' as a con. ATTACK SPEED DOES ALMOST NOTHING. The class doc states plainly that additional attack speed is mostly useless, because the macro is a fixed two-cast unit rather than a keydown or a spammable single cast. Do not recommend the attack speed Inner Ability line or attack-speed gearing for this class. WSE: for GMS Heroic the class doc's ideal weapon/secondary/emblem potential split is 9 ATT lines / 0 Boss / 0 IED, with 8/1/0 close behind, and it notes IED falls off sharply in value by mid-to-late game. It advises only chasing optimal lines on permanent equipment - Genesis Ancient Bow, Princess No's Immortal Relic, Mitra's Rage - once the rest of the gear is largely finished. Best-in-slot secondary is Princess No's Immortal Relic, but the doc says it is only marginally better than a level 100 secondary, so non-main characters can settle. RINGS: the doc ranks Ring of Restraint and Continuous Ring as similar on paper with RoR easier to use in practice, ahead of Whisper of the Source, ahead of a 22-star stat ring; for Heroic it recommends RoR outright with a WJ for swapping. LEGION GRID: the doc's bossing weighting is Critical Damage > Boss Damage / IED > Critical Rate > DEX > ATT, with the note that ATT is worth much less per block (1 ATT per block versus 5 DEX per block). The KMS wiki independently lists the same block families - Shade/Hayato/Mo Xuan for critical damage, Marksman/Night Lord for critical rate, Mercedes for cooldown reduction, Kanna/Demon Avenger for boss damage, the DEX archers for main stat - and singles out critical rate as especially important for Archers precisely because of the Vicious Shot conversion. ERDA NOVA MATTERS MORE THAN USUAL: because most of the burst damage comes from three limited-range summons, the class doc says a bind is needed to guarantee the burst lands, and tells boss-mule builders to take Erda Nova to level 20 or higher for any boss they cannot kill in one burst. It also records the interaction that bosses cannot be rebound for 90 seconds after a bind ends, so a level 25 Erda Nova's 120s cooldown aligns with the burst, and a Mercedes legion block enables a level 30 Erda Nova at 100s to come up before the boss's internal rebind timer expires.

commonMistakes.mistake: Treating Critical Rate as capped at 100% and redirecting points elsewhere
commonMistakes.why: Vicious Shot converts total critical rate, including the excess above 100%, into critical damage. Overflow critical rate is still damage on this class.
The class doc states that additional attack speed is mostly useless because of how the two-cast macro works, and lists minimal attack speed scaling as a class con.

commonMistakes.mistake: Manually alternating Cardinal Burst and Cardinal Deluge on two keys instead of using the macro or Auto Mode
commonMistakes.why: The class doc says the macro reaches the theoretical maximum output and manual alternation cannot beat it, and its current recommendation is actually Auto Mode (right-click Cardinal Burst to lock it) rather than the macro, because Auto Mode gets similar results with less precise inputs.

commonMistakes.mistake: Bursting without a bind and losing summon damage
commonMistakes.why: Three of the four burst components are summons with limited range. The class doc treats Erda Nova as necessary to guarantee full burst damage and gives explicit bind timing depending on whether the Origin skill is used.

commonMistakes.mistake: Firing Nova Blast without a full Relic Gauge
commonMistakes.why: Nova Blast's damage scales with the gauge consumed; the class doc says a full 1000/1000 gauge gives +100% final damage and 100% IED, and instructs pausing briefly before casting so the gauge fills.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming Cardinal Burst charges the Relic Gauge whenever it damages something
commonMistakes.why: The class doc records that Cardinal Burst must hit an enemy directly; the area-of-effect explosion at maximum range does not charge the gauge. This is the usual cause of unexpectedly running dry on gauge.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rolling Inner Ability outside a 50% Honor cost event, or min-maxing the Unique lines too early
commonMistakes.why: The class doc gives both as direct instructions - roll only during 50% events, and settle for any usable line in early and mid game rather than chasing Unique Critical Rate.

commonMistakes.mistake: Copying a five-pick hyper passive list from an aggregator
commonMistakes.why: Only three of the five Pathfinder hyper passives are unconditional. The other two depend on the character's IED relative to a 98.2% threshold and on the cooldown hat. A static list is wrong for two of the three documented cases.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving Curse Enchant Force unset while bossing
commonMistakes.why: The class doc says to lock the Burst (left) mode for bossing so Enchant Force skills stop following the emblem, and to lock Deluge (up) for mobbing to get the largest Combo Assault, or Torrent (right) for the turret form of Relic Unbound.

commonMistakes.mistake: Building all nine boost nodes before checking which seven the Mastery cores actually gate
commonMistakes.why: Only seven skills feed Mastery cores. Swarm Shot and Triple Impact do not. The class doc and the KMS wiki agree on this, and the doc gives a five-node arrangement that covers the seven required skills for players who want the matrix slot back. That said, the doc's own default advice is still to boost everything if reaching 6th job, because it is cheap on this class.

skillNameReference.validatedAgainst: https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Pathfinder/Skills (page last edited 2026-09-09, the v.271 patch date)
namingWarnings: The in-game wiki string for the Mastery skills is the 'HEXA <skill>' form; the class doc and community write them as '<skill> VI'. Same skills.

Mastery core 4's third component is 'Manifest Curse' in GMS. The class doc uses 'Relic Materialize' in its HEXA order section (which is the KMS string) and 'Manifest Curse' in its skill breakdown. Emit Manifest Curse.
The class doc writes the hyper passive as 'Cardinal Force - Bountiful Enhance'; the KMS wiki's translated string is 'Cardinal Force - Additional Enhancement'. Same passive.

MSEA localisation differs substantially (Cardinal Discharge, Cardinal Blast, Cardinal Transition, Split Mistel, Edge of Resonance, Relic Evolution, Ultimate Blast). The class doc carries its own GMS-to-MSEA mapping table. Do not mix regional strings.

sources.what: The Pathfinder class doc - a web-published Google Doc owned by the Pathfinder Mains Discord. Document currently owned by Naicha with additional maintenance by Ari; started by Jay MS, original formatting by Aerinaie, with named contributors Vincent (IGN Pathfinder), CloudAeris, Ovi-1 kan-ovi, Elysviel, Harry and RandomOnset. It is the only source that covers every field this file needs: boost node composition and leveling, node slot order by level, HEXA mastery/enhancement/common breakdown, HEXA leveling order, HEXA Stat by server type, hyper skill passives with a conditional rule, hyper stat guidance, Inner Ability with a full rolling strategy, WSE, cooldown hat, legion grid and artifact, burst rotation and mechanics. Read in full this session through a browser - note that a plain fetcher returns only base64 image data for this URL and the earlier survey concluded it was unreadable; it is readable, the browser renders the text layer.
sources.dated: Header reads 'Updated as of 1/8/26' but the changelog's most recent entry is 2026-03-30 - the header is stale relative to the body. Post-dates the GMS March 2026 balance patch, which it discusses; predates v.271 by roughly five months.

sources.what: Grandis Library Pathfinder page. Class properties, link skill, legion effect, boost node groupings bucketed Primary/Secondary/Other, a flat five-pick hyper passive build, recommended Inner Ability split bossing/training, and an explanation of the Relic Gauge. Read directly this session. Its credits block reads 'Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build: Class Doc', so for exactly those three fields it restates the class doc above and must not be counted as a second opinion. It IS usable as an independent check on class properties, link skill and legion effect, which come from its own data pipeline.
sources.dated: GMS Ver. 269 [Ride the Lightning Update] - two patches behind the v.271 target

sources.what: mastermysty's cross-class boost node trio reference. Lists Pathfinder's three trios explicitly, with no bossing/mobbing split. Independently authored, outside the class doc lineage. Read directly this session; its Pathfinder trios match the class doc's trio composition exactly, differing only in the order the three skills are written.
sources.dated: Page states last update 2024-11-21, with underlying testing data from 2024-05-14 - post-6th-job but predating the Mastery 3/4 rollout that the class doc says changed how these trios should be read

sources.what: NamuWiki's Pathfinder class page (Korean community wiki, machine-translated). Carries a genuine judgement section - Legion block recommendations with reasons, and a detailed Inner Ability section that argues line by line, including the specific claim that the cooldown-skip line only became a priority after 6th job and why. This is the only source found that corroborates the class doc's Inner Ability reasoning from outside the GMS class-doc lineage. Read directly this session. Caveat: KMS balance and KMS gear assumptions, no Reboot fragment economy.

NamuWiki's Pathfinder skill page. Independently confirms the four Mastery core groupings and, critically, confirms which boost nodes are 'essential' versus 'optional' - it marks Swarm Shot and Triple Impact as discretionary and the other seven as required, matching the GMS class doc. Also documents that Raven Tempest / Evolve Tempest have been REMOVED and replaced, and lists a third skill core beyond Forsaken Relic and Piercing Relic. Same source family as the page above; count the two NamuWiki pages as one source.

GMS-facing skill table. Used here strictly as a name-validation allowlist and for link skill numbers - it carries no judgement, no priority order and no recommendation. Confirms the Origin and Ascent skill names, all Mastery and Enhancement node names, and resolved the Manifest Curse versus Relic Materialize naming question. Returns HTTP 403 to a plain fetcher; read through a browser.
sources.dated: Page last edited 2026-09-09 - the v.271 patch date, making it the most current source in this set

sources.what: Pathfinder Mains Discord, linked from the class doc's own Additional Resources section. This is where the doc is maintained and where its maintainers (xlaicha, ari.ty) take corrections, so it is upstream of the class doc rather than a second source. Not machine-readable. Anything that changed after 2026-03-30 - in particular the Tempest rework flagged in conflicts - would land here first.

Cross-class Inner Ability aggregator by Samuel Franklin. Recorded ONLY because it dissents on Pathfinder's top line and the brief requires conflicts to be logged rather than quietly dropped. It gives no Pathfinder-specific reasoning, cites no class source, and links a generic inner ability simulator; its recommendation looks like a class-agnostic default. Treat as low reliability and do not let it outweigh the two lanes that agree against it.

Korean-built character power calculator. Not read directly for this class, but named here because the class doc credits its HEXA leveling order chart to MapleScouter and defers both hyper stat allocation and late HEXA Stat optimisation to it. This means the one available Pathfinder HEXA order is downstream of this tool, not independent analysis - relevant to how much confidence the app should express.

conflicts.topic: The Tempest skill appears to have been reworked and renamed, and the class doc has not caught up
positions: Class doc (changelog to 2026-03-30) and Grandis Library (GMS v269): the 5th job skill is Raven Tempest, it can only be used while Shadow Raven or Fury of the Wild is summoned, and Fury of the Wild is what enables the faster, shorter Evolved Tempest.

maplestorywiki.net (page edited 2026-09-09) and NamuWiki (2026-09-03): the skills are Storm Rider (a toggle that selects the storm's nature), Ancient Tempest and Primal Tempest, with no Raven summon requirement stated. NamuWiki lists 'Raven Tempest / Evolve Tempest' under a 'skills that have been removed' heading, and the corresponding enhancement node is named 'Ancient Tempest/Primal Tempest Boost' on both wikis.
conflicts.note: UNRESOLVED and potentially significant. If the rework is live in GMS v.271 then the class doc's burst rotation advice - summon the Raven first, keep Fury of the Wild up for Evolved Tempest - is stale, and its node leveling list (which names both Raven Tempest and Fury of the Wild) uses skill names that no longer exist. No patch note confirming or denying this could be found from this environment, and neither wiki page's history was checked. Do NOT display Raven Tempest or Fury of the Wild as current v.271 names without someone confirming in the Pathfinder Mains Discord. Everything else in this file is unaffected, because no priority claim here depends on the Tempest naming.

conflicts.topic: How often Glyph of Impalement VI procs its enhanced Ancient Impact version - now a THREE-way disagreement
positions: Class doc: "Every 5th cast of Glyph will result in an enhanced version, Ancient Impact."
KMS wiki (NamuWiki): "Edge of Resonance VI is strengthened with Ancient Impact every 4 times" (Edge of Resonance is the KMS name for Glyph of Impalement).

GMS wiki (maplestorywiki.net, edited on the v.271 patch date): the HEXA Glyph of Impalement skill text reads "Enhances Glyph of Impalement after being used 2 times", i.e. the 3rd cast is Ancient Impact.
conflicts.note: UPDATED 2026-09-12. The earlier version of this entry recorded only the 5-versus-4 split and said the wiki skill table gave no cast count; it does, and it agrees with neither. The GMS wiki's number is the one that describes GMS at v.271, but it is a single data table against a maintained GMS class doc, so this is recorded as contested rather than resolved. It matters for the cooldown-skip Inner Ability argument, because the value of extra Glyph casts depends on how many casts reach the enhanced version - a shorter counter makes cooldown skip better, not worse, so the argument's direction survives the disagreement even though its magnitude does not. Do NOT display a cast count as settled.

positions: Class doc and Grandis Library: 20% chance to skip cooldowns.
NamuWiki: agrees cooldown skip is a must-priority pick post-6th-job and recommends taking it at Legendary grade, while separately noting Boss Damage 20% is a generically good top line.
gameslikefinder.com: 20% Boss Damage top line, with abnormal-status damage and critical rate on the lower lines, and no cooldown skip anywhere.
conflicts.note: Recorded rather than resolved, per the brief, and re-checked 2026-09-12. The asymmetry is worth stating plainly: the two sources that dissent from gameslikefinder are a maintained class-owned document and a Korean wiki that independently arrives at the same mechanical reasoning (Ancient Impact on a cast counter plus Relic Materialize stacking per 50 gauge consumed), while gameslikefinder is a cross-class aggregator with no Pathfinder-specific argument and no cited class source, and Grandis Library - which agrees with the class doc - is a restatement of it rather than a third vote. Net: 2 independent lanes for cooldown skip, 1 aggregator against.

conflicts.topic: Hyper skill passive build presented as fixed versus conditional
positions: Grandis Library: a flat list of five - Cardinal Force Reinforce, Cardinal Force Bountiful Enhance, Cardinal Force Extra Strike, Ancient Force Boss Rush, Ancient Force Guardbreak.

Class doc: only three are unconditional, and the last two switch between Cardinal Force Reinforce, Ancient Force Guardbreak and Ancient Force Enchant Enhance depending on the character's IED (against a 98.2% threshold) and cooldown hat.
conflicts.note: Not a genuine disagreement so much as a loss of information in the restatement. Re-verified 2026-09-12: Grandis' five are exactly the class doc's answer for one of its three cases (IED below 98.2% with a -2s-or-less hat), and Grandis' own credits block reads "Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build: Class Doc", so the doc's conditional table is the better version of the same claim. Recorded because an aggregator-shaped flat list is what most tools will show.

conflicts.topic: Link skill effect at Master Level 9
positions: Grandis Library: Monster Collection chance +50%, Critical Rate +15%.
maplestorywiki.net: the same two plus Damage +6%, unlocked at Lv. 7, and a note that the Critical Rate bonus is multiplicative rather than additive.
conflicts.note: The wiki's version is more complete and more current (edited on the v.271 patch date). Most likely Grandis' page predates the damage component being added to the Explorer Archer link. Use the wiki's numbers.

conflicts.topic: The class doc's own stated date
positions: Document changelog: most recent entry dated 3/30/26, covering the GMS March 2026 balance patch, the Destiny Kaling update and revised cooldown hat / cooldown skip commentary.
conflicts.note: The body is newer than the header. Any pipeline that dates this source from the header line will under-rate it by roughly three months. Use 2026-03-30.

conflicts.topic: Whether the second boost node trio is a 'mobbing' trio
positions: mastermysty (2024-11-21): lists three Pathfinder trios with no bossing/mobbing labels at all - trio #1 Cardinal Deluge / Cardinal Burst / Glyph of Impalement, trio #2 Swarm Shot / Combo Assault / Cardinal Torrent, trio #3 Triple Impact / Shadow Raven / Ancient Astra.

Class doc: same three compositions, labelled "Bossing (high priority)" / "Mobbing" / "Tertiary", but states in writing that "The old classification of 'Mobbing' trio is no longer accurate, but kept for posterity", because Combo Assault's Mastery upgrade moved it into the bossing rotation and Cardinal Torrent and Ancient Astra are now boosted to satisfy Mastery core gates rather than for their own damage.

Grandis Library: does NOT publish trios. Its table lists which skills each of six nodes boosts, bucketed PRIMARY / SECONDARY / OTHER, which maps onto the four Mastery cores plus the two optional skills - not onto the trio composition.
conflicts.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-12. The earlier version of this entry credited Grandis Library with presenting the second trio; it does not present trios at all, and it has been removed from the trio sources throughout this file. The composition of all three trios is identical across the two lanes that do publish them (class doc, mastermysty), so node composition is well agreed at 2 independent lanes; only the rationale and labels have moved. Separately, Grandis' bucketing is itself stale: it defines SECONDARY as "Boost Nodes that don't unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery" and puts the Combo Assault / Shadow Raven node there, but that node unlocks Mastery 4 at v.271.

conflicts.topic: HEXA Mastery core investment order after M4
positions: Class doc (order credited to MapleScouter, published as an image): the first five investment steps are M4, M1, M2, M3, M3 - i.e. Combo Assault, then Cardinal Burst, then Cardinal Deluge, then Glyph/Torrent/Astra twice.
KMS wiki (NamuWiki skill page): "the priority for strengthening the Mastery Core is Combo Assault > Edge of Resonance > Cardinal Blast > Cardinal Discharge" - i.e. M4, then M3, then M1, then M2.
conflicts.note: NEW 2026-09-12. The two lanes agree that Mastery 4 (Combo Assault) is the first investment and disagree on the rest: the class doc puts the two macro halves ahead of Glyph, the KMS wiki puts Glyph second. That is why only the M4-first step in hexa.order is labelled moderate and the remaining steps stay weak. Plausible causes: the class doc's order is a Sol-Erda-Fragment-limited full-rotation optimisation from a calculator, while the KMS wiki's is an unweighted editorial ranking on KMS balance. Not resolvable from the public record.

gaps: HEXA investment order beyond the first five steps. The class doc's chart is an image; only its first five entries appear in the document's text layer. Reading the rest needs a vision pass over that image, which is the single highest-value follow-up for this class. The KMS wiki's four-core priority (M4 > M3 > M1 > M2) is now recorded as a partial second lane but covers only the four Mastery cores, not enhancement or skill cores.
Piercing Relic (the Ascent skill). Named by the GMS wiki, discussed by neither the class doc nor Grandis Library. No public source says where it belongs in the investment order.
A ranked hyper stat order. None exists publicly for this class and the class doc declines to invent one, pointing at MapleScouter. Left null deliberately, with both stat lists flagged unordered.
Reddit. r/Maplestory was unreachable from this environment in the research wave, so no reddit-side Pathfinder discussion was examined.

The Pathfinder Mains Discord. Not machine-readable. It is the only place that would confirm whether the Tempest rework flagged in conflicts is live in GMS v.271 and whether the class doc has been updated since 2026-03-30.

MapleGains (maplegains.com), a GMS-data HEXA optimiser, does NOT support Pathfinder as of the research wave - its class list was Battle Mage, Buccaneer, Cannon Master, Corsair, Mercedes, Mihile. Worth re-checking; it would be a genuinely independent HEXA-order lane if Pathfinder is added.

RESOLVED 2026-09-12 (kept here for the record): the KMS wiki's apparent THIRD skill core. Its GMS/MSEA/JMS name fields are blank and the GMS wiki, edited on the v.271 patch date, lists exactly two - Forsaken Relic (Origin) and Piercing Relic (Ascent). Treat GMS as having two.
researchNotes: Correction to the earlier source survey, worth propagating: the Pathfinder class doc was previously written off as unreadable because its body is base64-embedded images. That is true of what a markdown-converting fetcher sees, but the published Google Doc carries a full text layer. Two methods work: loading the /pub URL in a real browser and reading document.body.innerText, and - confirmed on 2026-09-12 and cheaper - plain curl with a browser User-Agent followed by stripping data:image/... URIs and tags, which yields the same roughly 100,000 characters including the changelog and credits. The same two wikis that return HTTP 403 to a markdown-converting fetcher (maplestorywiki.net, en.namu.wiki) both return HTTP 200 to curl with a browser User-Agent. Every source-backed claim in the five endgame sections of this file was re-read that way on 2026-09-12, not inferred from images. The same trick is worth trying on any other class doc previously marked image-only.

contest.method: Resolution pass over the five endgame sections (vMatrix, hexa, hyperSkills, hyperStats, innerAbility). NOTE: the adversarial wave recorded NO defects for Pathfinder - this file was absent from _contest-summary.json's filesBlocked list and carried no contest block, so there were zero inherited defects to settle. Instead of re-litigating nothing, every endgame claim was re-checked against the exact page it cites: the class doc, Grandis Library, mastermysty's node guide, both NamuWiki pages and the GMS wiki were all re-fetched and read in full on 2026-09-12. The defects below were found by that pass, not inherited.

resolved.claim: "The KMS wiki labels this node group the primary one."
resolved.finding: The KMS wiki's reinforcement-core table column that machine-translates to Primary / Secondary / tertiary / 4th / hyper is the JOB ADVANCEMENT TIER of each skill, not a priority ranking. Cardinal Deluge is the 1st job attack (hence "Primary") and Cardinal Burst is the 2nd job attack (hence "Secondary"). Confirmed by cross-reading the class doc's own skill-category table, which lists Cardinal Deluge (1st) and Cardinal Burst (2nd). The KMS wiki publishes no boost node priority order for this class.
resolved.action: CORRECTED - the claim was rewritten to say so explicitly, and the entry's consensus dropped from strong to moderate because the top-priority ranking now rests on two lanes (class doc, mastermysty) rather than three.

resolved.claim: Grandis Library cited as a source corroborating each of the three boost node trios.
resolved.finding: Grandis Library does not publish trios. Its "Skills Boosted by Each Nodes" table lists the contents of six nodes (Node 1 = Cardinal Burst + Bountiful Burst; Node 3 = Glyph + Cardinal Torrent + Ancient Astra; Node 4 = Combo Assault + Shadow Raven; Nodes 5 and 6 = Swarm Shot and Triple Impact), which is the Mastery-core grouping, not the trio composition. It also credits its boost node build to the class doc.
resolved.action: CORRECTED - Grandis removed from all three trio source lists; consensus dropped strong to moderate (2 independent lanes: class doc, mastermysty). A sourceCountNote on each trio records why.

resolved.claim: Grandis Library counted toward "strong" consensus on boost nodes, hyper passives and Inner Ability.
resolved.finding: Grandis' own credits block reads "Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build: Class Doc" - verified on the live page. For exactly those three fields it is a mirror of the class doc and must count once, not twice. The file's own sources block already said this, but the endgame sections were still counting it.
resolved.action: CORRECTED - sourceCount added to every endgame claim, counting independent lanes only, with sourceCountNote naming which sources were excluded and why. Several claims dropped from strong to moderate or weak as a result.

resolved.finding: The class doc says "bind Styx to AB activation". AB throughout this doc is the Angelic Buster link skill - it appears in the phrase "AB + Oz Ring", which the doc says should always be popped consecutively immediately before the burst skills. It is not Awakened Relic.
resolved.action: CORRECTED to Angelic Buster link activation, with the doc's own wording quoted.

resolved.claim: "Ancient Astra as the iframe / 60% damage reduction tool"; and "Epic Adventure is listed by the KMS wiki as the third hyper active".
resolved.finding: Per the GMS wiki, the 60% damage reduction belongs to Ancient Astra (Deluge) while channelling; the class doc's iframe note is about Ancient Astra in Burst mode, which it puts at 2s of iframe. And Epic Adventure is listed as a hyper active on BOTH wikis, not only the KMS one - what is true is that the class doc does not discuss it.
resolved.action: CORRECTED both; a fullActiveList sub-object was added recording the three hyper actives both wikis agree on.

resolved.finding: The KMS wiki independently states "the priority for strengthening the Mastery Core is Combo Assault > Edge of Resonance > Cardinal Blast > Cardinal Discharge" - Combo Assault (M4) first, matching the class doc's chart. That is a genuine second independent lane for the M4-first step only.
resolved.action: CONFIRMED and upgraded to moderate with sourceCount 2. The remaining steps stay weak, and the KMS wiki's disagreement about the order after M4 was logged as a new conflict.

resolved.claim: The level-40 boost gate was cited to the class doc, the KMS wiki and the GMS wiki with consensus "strong".
resolved.finding: Only the class doc states it: "In order to activate mastery nodes, the associated boost node level must total at least lvl 40 without matrix points." Neither wiki states a numeric gate. The four-core MEMBERSHIP, by contrast, genuinely is three-lane.
resolved.action: CORRECTED - the unlock rule now carries its own sources/sourceCount/consensus (class doc, 1, weak), while the core membership keeps strong at 3 lanes.

resolved.claim: "every fifth cast becomes an enhanced version, Ancient Impact", with the file noting only a 5-versus-4 split against the KMS wiki.
resolved.finding: The GMS wiki's own HEXA Glyph of Impalement text reads "Enhances Glyph of Impalement after being used 2 times" - the 3rd cast. That is a third distinct number, and it contradicts the file's earlier note that the wiki skill table gave no cast count.
resolved.action: CORRECTED - the hexa.order step now says "periodically" and points at the conflict; the conflict entry was rewritten as a three-way disagreement with all three quotations.

resolved.pattern: shape asserts what its source declines to
resolved.claim: bossingImportantStats and mobbingImportantStats shipped as bare arrays, which downstream code can read as ranked.
resolved.finding: The class doc introduces both lists as "the most important stats as a rule of thumb" and gives exactly one allocation rule - bring them all to level 10 before pushing one further. It publishes no ranking and explicitly defers to MapleScouter.
resolved.action: CORRECTED - an `ordered: false` flag plus an `orderedNote` were added stating that array position carries no priority meaning. `priority` stays null.

resolved.claim: "The KMS wiki lists a THIRD skill core beyond those two; whether GMS has it at v.271 was not confirmed."
resolved.finding: The KMS wiki's third entry has blank GMS/MSEA/JMS name fields, and the GMS wiki - page edited on the v.271 patch date - lists exactly two under its own headings, "Skill Node/Core 1 (Origin) Forsaken Relic" and "Skill Node/Core 2 (Ascent) Piercing Relic".
resolved.action: RESOLVED - GMS has two skill cores at v.271; the note and the gaps list were updated.

resolved.pattern: stale third-party bucket that would mislead
resolved.claim: No prior claim - this is an addition.
resolved.finding: Grandis Library defines its SECONDARY bucket as "Boost Nodes that don't unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery" and places the Combo Assault / Shadow Raven node there. At v.271 that node does unlock Mastery 4, confirmed by the class doc, the KMS wiki and the GMS wiki. Grandis is tagged GMS Ver. 269.
resolved.action: ADDED as an explicit caution on the Combo Assault entry and in the trio conflict, so the app never deprioritises that node on Grandis' authority.

resolved.claim: The V-skill node leveling order was class doc only.
resolved.finding: The KMS wiki gives its own V-skill enhancement order - "Ancient Tempest > Relic Unbound > Ultimate Blast > Obsidian Barrier", with a footnote inserting Critical Reinforce and Maple World Goddess' Blessing after Ancient Tempest. Both lanes put the Tempest skill first and Obsidian Barrier last; they disagree on where Nova Blast (Ultimate Blast) and Vicious Shot sit.
resolved.action: CONFIRMED at the ends, disagreement recorded in the notes text; notesSourceCount set to 2 with consensus moderate.

resolved.claim: "no cast time and can be fired during other skills' animations" and "the gauge regulator outside burst".
resolved.finding: Both are stated in the class doc's Glyph skill entry verbatim: "It can be cast even while in animation for other skills" and "Outside of burst, this is the main skill that helps you regulate the relic gauge."
resolved.action: CONFIRMED - claim kept, quotations added so it is checkable.

resolved.finding: Re-read verbatim in the class doc. Axes are CD Hat (-2s or less / -3s or more) against IED (< 98.2 / > 98.2); the > 98.2 row gives one answer spanning both hat columns. All three cases in this file match the table exactly, and all six passive names were validated against the GMS wiki's Hyper Skills table.
resolved.action: CONFIRMED - kept as-is, labelled weak because it exists in exactly one source.

resolved.claim: Cooldown skip top line, Unique Critical Rate, Unique Boss Damage with abnormal-status settle.
resolved.finding: All three re-read in the class doc's Inner Ability table and in the KMS wiki's ability section, and every mechanical reason attributed to the KMS wiki was found there in those words - cooldown skip being poor pre-6th-job and a must after it, Legendary over Unique because Unique resets poorly, critical rate paying past 100% via Critical Reinforce and being worth about 10% critical damage, and the abnormal-status line being easy to keep up via the Ancient Curse debuff or the Explorer Mage link.
resolved.action: CONFIRMED at moderate (2 independent lanes), with Grandis explicitly excluded from the count.

outOfScope: skillBuilds for jobs 1-4 - left untouched per the product owner's scope note.

Skill damage coefficients and damageLine - left untouched, except where a coefficient appears inside an endgame rationale (Combo Assault VI 7930% to 30132%, Glyph 10740% / Ancient Impact 16110%), which were re-read in the class doc and found accurate.
Burst rotation, keybinds and boss-by-boss tips - out of the five endgame sections.
gearingNotes, commonMistakes, linkSkill and legionEffect - not in scope for this pass and left as the research wave wrote them, except that no claim in them was promoted or demoted.
contest.shipReadyNote: Every claim in the five endgame sections now names the page that supports it, was re-read against that page on 2026-09-12, and carries sourceCount counting independent lanes only. Four claims were corrected for citation inversion or misreading, one data shape was flagged unordered, one gap was closed, one claim was upgraded on new corroboration, and nothing was left pointing at a source that does not support it. Nothing was deleted outright - no fabricated node or skill name was found in this file, and every disputed name resolved to a real GMS or KMS string.

v271Reconcile.note: This guide was written and resolved BEFORE the v.271 patch notes were readable, so its skill names predate them. A name the patch removed is not stale, it is wrong - a player would go looking for a skill that no longer exists.

blockedReason: References 1 skill name(s) removed in v.271 (Raven Tempest). Needs a pass against the v.271 notes before it can be shown.
